pattern: 〜まで
meaning: Until, as far as: marks where a time, a distance or a range ends. Often paired with から (from).

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}9{時|じ}から5{時|じ}[[まで]]{働|はたら}きます。
examples.en: I work from nine to five every day.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}[[まで]]{歩|ある}いて10{分|ぷん}です。
examples.en: It's a ten-minute walk to the station.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みは{来週|らいしゅう}の{金曜日|きんようび}[[まで]]です。
examples.en: The summer holidays last until next Friday.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{夜遅|よるおそ}く[[まで]]{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.en: Yesterday I studied until late at night.

questions.ja: {朝|あさ}から{晩|ばん}[[まで]]{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていました。
questions.en: It rained from morning till night.
questions.explain: から〜まで marks a span: from one point until another.

questions.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{来|く}る[[まで]]、ここで{待|ま}ちましょう。
questions.en: Let's wait here until the train comes.
questions.explain: まで goes with an action that lasts up to a point, like waiting; までに means 'by' a deadline.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + 前に / Noun + の前に
meaning: Before: the first action happens before the second. The verb before 前に stays in dictionary form even in a past sentence; nouns take の前に.

examples.ja: {寝|ね}る[[{前|まえ}に]]{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
examples.en: I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

examples.ja: {食|た}べる[[{前|まえ}に]]{手|て}を{洗|あら}いましょう。
examples.en: Let's wash our hands before we eat.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}へ{来|く}る[[{前|まえ}に]]、{少|すこ}し{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.en: I studied a little Japanese before I came to Japan.

examples.ja: {授業|じゅぎょう}の[[{前|まえ}に]]{宿題|しゅくだい}を{出|だ}してください。
examples.en: Please hand in your homework before class.

questions.ja: {昨日|きのう}は[[{寝|ね}る]]{前|まえ}に{少|すこ}し{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みました。
questions.en: Last night I read a little before going to sleep.
questions.explain: 前に always follows the dictionary form, even when the sentence is in the past.

questions.ja: {家|いえ}を{出|で}る[[{前|まえ}に]]、{電気|でんき}を{消|け}します。
questions.en: I turn off the lights before I leave the house.
questions.explain: Dictionary form + 前に means 'before doing'; 前で is a place, 'in front of'.

pattern: Verb-stem + ませんか
meaning: Won't you…? / Would you like to…?: a polite, soft invitation that makes it easy for the other person to say no.

examples.ja: {一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: Would you like to see a film together?

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}、{公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}し[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: How about a walk in the park on Sunday?

examples.ja: ちょっと{休|やす}み[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: Why don't we take a short break?

examples.ja: {今晩|こんばん}、うちでご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[ませんか]]。
examples.en: Would you like to have dinner at my place tonight?

questions.ja: {明日|あした}、{一緒|いっしょ}に{図書館|としょかん}へ[[{行|い}きませんか]]。
questions.en: Would you like to go to the library with me tomorrow?
questions.explain: ませんか attaches to the ます-stem (行き), and an invitation about tomorrow can't be past.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}の{家|いえ}に{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}[[ませんか]]。
questions.en: Would you like to come over to my place?
questions.explain: Only the listener can come to the speaker's home, so it has to be an invitation: ませんか.

pattern: Verb-stem + ましょう
meaning: Let's…: a polite way to suggest doing something together, or to agree to a plan someone has offered.

examples.ja: もう{遅|おそ}いですから、{帰|かえ}り[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: It's late, so let's go home.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}の{前|まえ}で{会|あ}い[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's meet in front of the station.

examples.ja: {一緒|いっしょ}に{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{作|つく}り[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's make dinner together.

examples.ja: {次|つぎ}の{問題|もんだい}をやり[[ましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's do the next question.

questions.ja: 「{一緒|いっしょ}に{帰|かえ}りませんか。」「ええ、{帰|かえ}り[[ましょう]]。」
questions.en: "Shall we go home together?" "Yes, let's."
questions.explain: To say yes to an invitation, answer with ましょう: 'yes, let's'.

questions.ja: では、10ページを[[{読|よ}みましょう]]。
questions.en: Right, let's read page 10.
questions.explain: ましょう attaches to the ます-stem: 読む becomes 読み.

pattern: Verb-stem + ましょうか
meaning: Shall I…? / Shall we…?: offers to do something for someone, or asks what to do together.

examples.ja: その{荷物|にもつ}、{持|も}ち[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: Shall I carry that bag for you?

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}いですね。{窓|まど}を{開|あ}け[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: It's hot, isn't it? Shall I open the window?

examples.ja: どこで{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: Where shall we have lunch?

examples.ja: {写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}り[[ましょうか]]。
examples.en: Shall I take a photo of you?

questions.ja: {私|わたし}が{窓|まど}を{閉|し}め[[ましょうか]]。
questions.en: Shall I close the window?
questions.explain: With 私が the speaker is offering to do it, so ましょうか fits.

questions.ja: {何時|なんじ}に{駅|えき}で{会|あ}い[[ましょうか]]。
questions.en: What time shall we meet at the station?
questions.explain: A question word plus ましょうか asks the other person to help decide a plan.

pattern: Noun + も
meaning: Too, also; with a negative, (not) either. It takes the place of は, が or を. A question word + も + negative means nobody or nothing.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}[[も]]コーヒーが{好|す}きです。
examples.en: I like coffee too.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{肉|にく}も{魚|さかな}[[も]]{食|た}べません。
examples.en: My older brother eats neither meat nor fish.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{何|なに}[[も]]{食|た}べませんでした。
examples.en: I didn't eat anything yesterday.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}で1{時間|じかん}[[も]]{待|ま}ちました。
examples.en: I waited at the station for a whole hour.

questions.ja: {部屋|へや}には{誰|だれ}[[も]]いませんでした。
questions.en: There was nobody in the room.
questions.explain: Question word + も + a negative verb means 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

questions.ja: {父|ちち}も{母|はは}[[も]]{元気|げんき}です。
questions.en: Both my father and my mother are well.
questions.explain: AもBも means 'both A and B'; the second noun takes も as well.

pattern: もう + Verb
meaning: Already, with a finished action; not … any more, with a negative. Before an amount it means 'more': もう一つ, もう少し.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}は[[もう]]{終|お}わりました。
examples.en: I've already finished my homework.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}は[[もう]]{出|で}ましたか。
examples.en: Has the train already left?

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は[[もう]]たばこを{吸|す}いません。
examples.en: My father doesn't smoke any more.

examples.ja: [[もう]]{一|ひと}つください。
examples.en: One more, please.

questions.ja: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}は[[もう]]{食|た}べましたか。
questions.en: Have you had lunch yet?
questions.explain: もう with a past verb asks whether something has already happened; まだ, あまり and ぜんぜん don't fit a finished action.

questions.ja: すみません、[[もう]]{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}してください。
questions.en: Excuse me, could you speak a little more slowly?
questions.explain: もう少し is the set way to say 'a little more'.

pattern: な-adjective + な + Noun / な-adjective + です
meaning: Adjectives like 静か, 有名 and 便利. They take な before a noun and work like nouns at the end of a sentence: 静かです, 静かじゃない, 静かでした.

examples.ja: {静|しず}か[[な]]{町|まち}に{住|す}みたいです。
examples.en: I want to live in a quiet town.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}はあまりきれい[[じゃない]]です。
examples.en: This room isn't very clean.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}の{公園|こうえん}はとてもにぎやか[[でした]]。
examples.en: The park was really lively on Sunday.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{魚|さかな}が{嫌|きら}い[[じゃありません]]。
examples.en: I don't dislike fish.

questions.ja: ここは{有名|ゆうめい}[[な]]レストランです。
questions.en: This is a famous restaurant.
questions.explain: A な-adjective takes な before a noun.

questions.ja: {先週|せんしゅう}は{仕事|しごと}が{大変|たいへん}[[でした]]。
questions.en: Work was tough last week.
questions.explain: In the past, a な-adjective takes でした, like a noun; かった is for い-adjectives.

pattern: Plain form + なあ
meaning: A casual exclamation or sigh, often said to yourself: 'Wow…', 'Man…'. After たい it sounds wistful: 'I'd love to…'.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}のケーキ、おいしい[[なあ]]。
examples.en: The cake at this place is so good.

examples.ja: {仕事|しごと}が{忙|いそが}しい[[なあ]]。
examples.en: Man, work is busy.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{行|い}きたい[[なあ]]。
examples.en: I'd really love to go to Japan.

examples.ja: {大|おお}きい{家|いえ}だ[[なあ]]。
examples.en: What a big house!

questions.ja: いい{天気|てんき}[[だなあ]]。
questions.en: What lovely weather.
questions.explain: After a noun, なあ needs だ in front of it: 天気だなあ.

questions.ja: この{部屋|へや}、[[{寒|さむ}いなあ]]。
questions.en: This room is freezing.
questions.explain: An い-adjective takes なあ straight after い, with no だ.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + ないで
meaning: Without doing: you do the main action and skip the first one, like going out without an umbrella.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[ないで]]{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}きました。
examples.en: I went to school without eating breakfast.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}を{持|も}た[[ないで]]{出|で}かけました。
examples.en: I went out without an umbrella.

examples.ja: {辞書|じしょ}を{使|つか}わ[[ないで]]この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みました。
examples.en: I read this book without using a dictionary.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{寝|ね}[[ないで]]{勉強|べんきょう}しました。
examples.en: Yesterday I studied without sleeping.

questions.ja: {歯|は}を{磨|みが}か[[ないで]]{寝|ね}ました。
questions.en: I went to bed without brushing my teeth.
questions.explain: ないで joins a skipped action to the main verb: 'without doing'.

questions.ja: {何|なに}も[[{言|い}わないで]]{帰|かえ}りました。
questions.en: He went home without saying anything.
questions.explain: 言う is a godan verb, so its ない-form is 言わない; なくて can't mean 'without'.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + ないでください
meaning: Please don't…: a polite request asking someone not to do something.

examples.ja: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ら[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't take photos here.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}で{食|た}べ[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't eat in the classroom.

examples.ja: この{話|はなし}は{誰|だれ}にも{言|い}わ[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't tell anyone about this.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{授業|じゅぎょう}を{忘|わす}れ[[ないでください]]。
examples.en: Please don't forget tomorrow's class.

questions.ja: {危|あぶ}ないですから、この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}が[[ないでください]]。
questions.en: It's dangerous, so please don't swim in this river.
questions.explain: The polite 'please don't' is the ない-form + でください.

questions.ja: ここは{図書館|としょかん}ですから、{大|おお}きい{声|こえ}で[[{話|はな}さないでください]]。
questions.en: This is a library, so please don't talk loudly.
questions.explain: 話す is a godan verb: its ない-form is 話さない.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + ないといけない
meaning: Have to, must: literally 'if I don't, it won't do'. Very common in everyday speech.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は6{時|じ}に{起|お}き[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I have to get up at six tomorrow.

examples.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}ま[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I have to take my medicine.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{部屋|へや}を{掃除|そうじ}し[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I need to clean my room today.

examples.ja: もう{帰|かえ}ら[[ないといけません]]。
examples.en: I have to go home now.

questions.ja: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}は{早|はや}いですから、{今日|きょう}は{早|はや}く{寝|ね}[[ないといけません]]。
questions.en: I have an early start tomorrow, so I have to go to bed early tonight.
questions.explain: The pattern is the ない-form + と + いけません.

questions.ja: {財布|さいふ}を{忘|わす}れました。{家|いえ}に[[{帰|かえ}らないといけません]]。
questions.en: I've left my wallet behind. I have to go back home.
wrong: {帰|かえ}りないといけません
{帰|かえ}るないといけません
questions.explain: 帰る looks like an ichidan verb but is godan, so its ない-form is 帰らない.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくてもいい(です)
meaning: Don't have to, needn't: says that something isn't necessary.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{学校|がっこう}へ{来|こ}[[なくてもいいです]]。
examples.en: You don't have to come to school tomorrow.

examples.ja: {靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}が[[なくてもいいです]]よ。
examples.en: You don't need to take your shoes off.

examples.ja: {全部|ぜんぶ}は{食|た}べ[[なくてもいいです]]。
examples.en: You don't have to eat all of it.

examples.ja: {名前|なまえ}は{書|か}か[[なくてもいい]]ですか。
examples.en: Is it all right if I don't write my name?

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}ですから、{早|はや}く{起|お}き[[なくてもいいです]]。
questions.en: It's Sunday today, so I don't have to get up early.
questions.explain: 'Don't have to' is the ない-form with い dropped + くてもいい.

questions.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていませんから、{傘|かさ}は[[{持|も}たなくてもいいです]]よ。
questions.en: It isn't raining, so you don't need to take an umbrella.
questions.explain: 持つ is godan: 持たない becomes 持たなくてもいい.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくちゃ
meaning: Gotta, have to: a casual spoken shortening of なくては(いけない). The いけない part is usually left off.

examples.ja: あ、もう8{時|じ}だ。{行|い}か[[なくちゃ]]。
examples.en: Oh, it's already eight. I've got to go.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}テストだから、{勉強|べんきょう}し[[なくちゃ]]。
examples.en: I've got a test tomorrow, so I need to study.

examples.ja: {牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}がない。{買|か}わ[[なくちゃ]]。
examples.en: We're out of milk. I need to buy some.

examples.ja: {母|はは}に{電話|でんわ}し[[なくちゃ]]いけない。
examples.en: I have to call my mum.

questions.ja: もう{遅|おそ}いから、{帰|かえ}ら[[なくちゃ]]。
questions.en: It's late, so I've got to head home.
questions.explain: なくちゃ is a squeezed なくては: the ない-form with い dropped + くちゃ.

questions.ja: {明日|あした}は{早|はや}く[[{起|お}きなくちゃ]]。
questions.en: I've got to get up early tomorrow.
questions.explain: 起きる is ichidan: drop る to get 起きない, then 起きなくちゃ.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくてはいけない
meaning: Must, have to: something is required, by a rule or by the situation.

examples.ja: {学生|がくせい}は{宿題|しゅくだい}をし[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: Students have to do their homework.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}の{本|ほん}を{返|かえ}さ[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: I have to return the library books.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}では{家|いえ}に{入|はい}る{時|とき}、{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}が[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: In Japan you have to take your shoes off when you go into a house.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}はこの{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}か[[なくてはいけません]]。
examples.en: I have to write this letter today.

questions.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}る{時|とき}は、{切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}わ[[なくてはいけません]]。
questions.en: You have to buy a ticket when you take the train.
questions.explain: 'Must' is the ない-form with い dropped + くてはいけません.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}も{仕事|しごと}を[[しなくてはいけません]]。
questions.en: I have to work on Sundays too.
wrong: さなくてはいけません
すなくてはいけません
しなくてもいけません
questions.explain: The ない-form of する is しない, so it becomes しなくてはいけません.

pattern: Verb (ない-form) + なくてはならない
meaning: Must, have to: means the same as なくてはいけない but sounds stiffer. Used for duties and rules, and in writing.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}は{学校|がっこう}へ{行|い}か[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: Children must go to school.

examples.ja: {外国|がいこく}へ{行|い}く{時|とき}は、パスポートを{持|も}って{行|い}か[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: When you travel abroad, you must take your passport.

examples.ja: {会社|かいしゃ}には9{時|じ}に{着|つ}か[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: I have to be at the office at nine.

examples.ja: {借|か}りたお{金|かね}は{返|かえ}さ[[なくてはなりません]]。
examples.en: Money you borrow must be paid back.

questions.ja: {病院|びょういん}の{中|なか}では{静|しず}かにし[[なくてはなりません]]。
questions.en: You must keep quiet inside the hospital.
questions.explain: The pattern ends in なりません, the polite negative of なる.

questions.ja: {次|つぎ}のバスまで、ここで[[{待|ま}たなくてはなりません]]。
questions.en: I have to wait here until the next bus.
wrong: {待|ま}ちなくてはなりません
{待|ま}つなくてはなりません
{待|ま}たないてはなりません
questions.explain: 待つ is godan: 待たない becomes 待たなくてはなりません.

pattern: Noun / な-adjective + になる, い-adjective (〜く) + なる
meaning: To become: shows a change. Nouns and な-adjectives take に (医者になる, 静かになる); い-adjectives change い to く (暗くなる).

examples.ja: {春|はる}になって、{暖|あたた}か[[くなりました]]。
examples.en: Spring has come and it's got warmer.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{医者|いしゃ}[[になりました]]。
examples.en: My older brother became a doctor.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}を{掃除|そうじ}して、きれい[[になりました]]。
examples.en: I cleaned the room and now it's tidy.

examples.ja: {来月|らいげつ}、20{歳|さい}[[になります]]。
examples.en: I'll turn twenty next month.

questions.ja: {夕方|ゆうがた}、{空|そら}が{暗|くら}[[くなりました]]。
questions.en: In the evening the sky got dark.
questions.explain: An い-adjective changes い to く before なる: 暗い becomes 暗くなる.

questions.ja: {子供|こども}たちが{寝|ね}て、{家|いえ}が{静|しず}か[[になりました]]。
questions.en: The children went to sleep and the house went quiet.
questions.explain: A な-adjective takes に before なる: 静かになる.

pattern: Plain form + んです (Noun / な-adjective + なんです)
meaning: Explains, or asks about, the reason or background: 'the thing is…', 'is it that…?'. Conversational; nouns and な-adjectives take なんです.

examples.ja: {頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い[[んです]]。
examples.en: I've got a headache, you see.

examples.ja: どうして{食|た}べない[[んですか]]。
examples.en: Why aren't you eating?

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{誕生日|たんじょうび}な[[んです]]。
examples.en: It's my birthday today, actually.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はパーティーに{行|い}きませんでした。{仕事|しごと}が{忙|いそが}しかった[[んです]]。
examples.en: I didn't go to the party yesterday. Work was busy.

questions.ja: {遅|おそ}くなってすみません。{電車|でんしゃ}が{来|こ}なかった[[んです]]。
questions.en: Sorry I'm late. The train didn't come.
questions.explain: After a verb, んです attaches directly; な is only for nouns and な-adjectives.

questions.ja: {今日|きょう}は{遊|あそ}びません。{明日|あした}テスト[[なんです]]。
questions.en: I'm not going out today. I've got a test tomorrow.
questions.explain: A noun needs な before んです: テストなんです.

pattern: Sentence + ね
meaning: Right? / isn't it?: looks for agreement or checks something both people know. It also softens a remark or fills a pause (そうですね…).

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}はいい{天気|てんき}です[[ね]]。
examples.en: Lovely weather today, isn't it?

examples.ja: このケーキ、おいしいです[[ね]]。
examples.en: This cake is delicious, isn't it?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は10{時|じ}です[[ね]]。
examples.en: It's at ten tomorrow, right?

examples.ja: マリアさんは{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}です[[ね]]。
examples.en: Your Japanese is really good, Maria.

questions.ja: 「この{店|みせ}、{安|やす}いですね。」「ええ、{本当|ほんとう}に{安|やす}いです[[ね]]。」
questions.en: "This shop is cheap, isn't it?" "Yes, it really is."
questions.explain: When you agree with something you both see, end with ね.

questions.ja: 「{何|なに}を{飲|の}みますか。」「そうです[[ね]]、じゃあ、コーヒーにします。」
questions.en: "What will you have to drink?" "Let me see… I'll have coffee, then."
questions.explain: そうですね buys a moment to think before answering.

pattern: Noun + に
meaning: Marks a point: a time (7時に), where something is (机の上に), a destination, or the person you give to or meet.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}7{時|じ}[[に]]{起|お}きます。
examples.en: I get up at seven every morning.

examples.ja: {机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}[[に]]{本|ほん}があります。
examples.en: There's a book on the desk.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}[[に]]{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter to a friend.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}で{電車|でんしゃ}[[に]]{乗|の}りました。
examples.en: I got on the train at the station.

questions.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}11{時|じ}[[に]]{寝|ね}ます。
questions.en: I go to bed at eleven every night.
questions.explain: A clock time takes に.

questions.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{中|なか}[[に]]{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}があります。
questions.en: There's milk in the fridge.
questions.explain: With あります and います, the place where something is takes に.

pattern: Verb-stem + に行く / Noun + に行く
meaning: Go somewhere to do something: the purpose (a verb stem or an activity noun) comes before に and a verb of movement.

examples.ja: {公園|こうえん}へ{遊|あそ}び[[に{行|い}きます]]。
examples.en: I'm going to the park to play.

examples.ja: デパートへ{服|ふく}を{買|か}い[[に{行|い}きました]]。
examples.en: I went to the department store to buy clothes.

examples.ja: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ[[に{行|い}きませんか]]。
examples.en: Do you want to go and get lunch?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{買|か}い{物|もの}[[に{行|い}きます]]。
examples.en: I'm going shopping tomorrow.

questions.ja: {郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}へ{切手|きって}を{買|か}い[[に]]{行|い}きます。
questions.en: I'm going to the post office to buy stamps.
questions.explain: Verb-stem + に shows the purpose of going.

questions.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}に{海|うみ}へ[[{泳|およ}ぎ]]に{行|い}きました。
questions.en: On Sunday I went to the sea to swim.
questions.explain: The purpose verb goes in its ます-stem: 泳ぐ becomes 泳ぎ.

pattern: Noun + にする
meaning: To decide on, go with: used when you choose something, such as ordering in a café or picking a day.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はコーヒー[[にします]]。
examples.en: I'll have coffee.

examples.ja: {誕生日|たんじょうび}のプレゼントは{花|はな}[[にしました]]。
examples.en: I went with flowers for the birthday present.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}は{来月|らいげつ}[[にしましょう]]。
examples.en: Let's make the trip next month.

examples.ja: {赤|あか}いのと{青|あお}いの、どちら[[にしますか]]。
examples.en: The red one or the blue one: which will you take?

questions.ja: {昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}は{何|なに}[[にします]]か。
questions.en: What are you going to have for lunch?
questions.explain: Choosing something is Noun + にする.

questions.ja: {飲|の}み{物|もの}はオレンジジュース[[にします]]。
questions.en: For my drink, I'll have orange juice.
questions.explain: When you pick from options, the choice takes にする.

pattern: Place + に / へ + verb of movement
meaning: Both mark where you're heading. へ points to the direction; に points to the arrival point and has other jobs, like times and people, that へ can't do.

examples.ja: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}[[へ]]{行|い}きます。
examples.en: I'm going to Japan next year.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}6{時|じ}に{家|いえ}[[に]]{帰|かえ}ります。
examples.en: I get home at six every day.

examples.ja: この{道|みち}を{北|きた}[[へ]]{行|い}ってください。
examples.en: Please go north along this road.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}は{昨日|きのう}アメリカ[[に]]{着|つ}きました。
examples.en: My friend arrived in America yesterday.

questions.ja: {駅|えき}で{先生|せんせい}[[に]]{会|あ}いました。
questions.en: I ran into my teacher at the station.
questions.explain: The person you meet with 会う takes に; へ only shows direction.

questions.ja: これは{母|はは}[[への]]{手紙|てがみ}です。
questions.en: This is a letter to my mother.
questions.explain: へ can take の to link to a noun (a letter to…); に can't.

pattern: Noun + の + Noun
meaning: Joins two nouns: whose it is (私の傘), or what kind or where from (日本語の先生). It can also stand for a noun already mentioned: 兄のです.

examples.ja: これは{私|わたし}[[の]]{傘|かさ}です。
examples.en: This is my umbrella.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}[[の]]{先生|せんせい}はとても{面白|おもしろ}いです。
examples.en: Our Japanese teacher is really fun.

examples.ja: その{青|あお}いかばんは{兄|あに}[[の]]です。
examples.en: That blue bag is my older brother's.

examples.ja: {大学|だいがく}[[の]]{友達|ともだち}と{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
examples.en: I saw a film with a friend from university.

questions.ja: あれはトムさん[[の]]{車|くるま}です。
questions.en: That's Tom's car.
questions.explain: の shows who something belongs to.

questions.ja: {学校|がっこう}[[の]]{前|まえ}に{本屋|ほんや}があります。
questions.en: There's a bookshop in front of the school.
questions.explain: Position words like 前 and 上 join the noun with の: 学校の前.

pattern: Plain form + のです (Noun / な-adjective + なのです)
meaning: Gives or asks for an explanation, like んです but fuller and more formal. Common in writing and careful speech.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}、トムさんは{会社|かいしゃ}を{休|やす}みます。{風邪|かぜ}を{引|ひ}いた[[のです]]。
examples.en: Tom is off work today. He has caught a cold.

examples.ja: この{村|むら}には{駅|えき}がありません。{村|むら}の{人|ひと}はバスで{町|まち}へ{行|い}く[[のです]]。
examples.en: This village has no station, so the people here go to town by bus.

examples.ja: どうして{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}している[[のですか]]。
examples.en: Why is it that you're studying Japanese?

examples.ja: {本当|ほんとう}は、{魚|さかな}が{嫌|きら}いな[[のです]]。
examples.en: The truth is, I don't like fish.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{毎朝|まいあさ}、{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}きます。{体|からだ}にいい[[のです]]。
questions.en: I walk to the station every morning. It's good for my health.
questions.explain: An い-adjective takes のです directly, with no な or だ.

questions.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}くて、とても{便利|べんり}[[なのです]]。
questions.en: This flat is close to the station, so it's very convenient.
questions.explain: A な-adjective keeps な before のです: 便利なのです.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + のが下手(です)
meaning: Bad at doing something. の turns the verb into a noun so it can take が下手.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{歌|うた}を{歌|うた}う[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: I'm bad at singing.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}る[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: My father is a bad cook.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}は{英語|えいご}を{話|はな}す[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: My older brother is bad at speaking English.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{人|ひと}の{名前|なまえ}を{覚|おぼ}える[[のが{下手|へた}]]です。
examples.en: I'm bad at remembering people's names.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{泳|およ}ぐ[[のが]]{下手|へた}です。
questions.en: I'm a poor swimmer.
questions.explain: A verb needs の before が下手: 泳ぐのが下手.

questions.ja: {妹|いもうと}は{漢字|かんじ}を[[{読|よ}む]]のが{下手|へた}です。
questions.en: My younger sister is bad at reading kanji.
questions.explain: The verb before のが stays in dictionary form.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + のが上手(です)
meaning: Good at doing something. Mostly said about other people; said about yourself it can sound like boasting.

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}る[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]です。
examples.en: My mother is a good cook.

examples.ja: ケンさんは{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}る[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]ですね。
examples.en: You take great photos, Ken.

examples.ja: {弟|おとうと}は{絵|え}をかく[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]です。
examples.en: My younger brother is good at drawing.

examples.ja: マリアさんは{英語|えいご}を{教|おし}える[[のが{上手|じょうず}]]です。
examples.en: Maria is good at teaching English.

questions.ja: {姉|あね}はピアノを{弾|ひ}く[[のが]]{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.en: My older sister plays the piano well.
questions.explain: 上手 takes が, so the verb phrase becomes 弾くのが.

questions.ja: リサさんは{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を[[{聞|き}く]]のが{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.en: Lisa is a good listener.
questions.explain: The verb before のが is in dictionary form.

pattern: Verb (dictionary form) + のが好き(です)
meaning: Like doing something. の turns the verb phrase into a noun so it can take が好き.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: I like reading books.

examples.ja: {妹|いもうと}は{犬|いぬ}と{遊|あそ}ぶ[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: My younger sister loves playing with the dog.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}に{公園|こうえん}を{歩|ある}く[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: I like walking in the park on Sundays.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{古|ふる}い{映画|えいが}を{見|み}る[[のが{好|す}き]]です。
examples.en: My father likes watching old films.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}く[[のが]]{好|す}きです。
questions.en: I like listening to music.
questions.explain: A verb needs の to become a noun before が好き.

questions.ja: {私|わたし}は{友達|ともだち}と[[{話|はな}す]]のが{好|す}きです。
questions.en: I like talking with my friends.
questions.explain: Dictionary form + のが好き: 話すのが好き.
